scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. A judge converts your summary suit into a regular suit. Can you appeal that order under the Commercial Courts Act?
On sixth October, a Delhi High Court Division Bench of Honourable Justice Dinesh Mehta and Honourable Doctor Justice Aditi Choudhary ruled.
scenes.shown: On 6 October, a Delhi High Court Division Bench of Honourable Justice Dinesh Mehta and Honourable Dr. Justice Aditi Choudhary ruled.

scenes.dialogue: Two coal transport firms, working with the Directorate General of Resettlement since twenty eighteen, disputed amounts deducted by Coal India and others.
scenes.shown: Two coal transport firms, working with the Directorate General of Resettlement since 2018, disputed amounts deducted by Coal India and others.

scenes.dialogue: They filed summary suits under Order Thirty Seven. In July, the Single Judge held its parameters were not met, and converted them into regular suits.
scenes.shown: They filed summary suits under Order XXXVII. In July, the Single Judge held its parameters were not met, and converted them into regular suits.

scenes.dialogue: They appealed under Section Thirteen of the Commercial Courts Act. Their counsel sought time on maintainability, but on the next two dates, no one appeared for them.
scenes.shown: They appealed under Section 13 of the Commercial Courts Act. Their counsel sought time on maintainability, but on the next two dates, no one appeared for them.

scenes.dialogue: The proviso to Section Thirteen One A says an appeal lies from orders listed in Order Forty Three, and Section Thirty Seven of the Arbitration Act.
scenes.shown: The proviso to Section 13(1A) says an appeal lies from orders listed in Order XLIII, and Section 37 of the Arbitration Act.

scenes.dialogue: In twenty seventeen, a coordinate bench held this restricts the appealable orders to only those specifically enumerated in Order Forty Three.
scenes.shown: In 2017, a coordinate bench held this restricts the appealable orders to only those specifically enumerated in Order XLIII.

scenes.dialogue: The Supreme Court affirmed this view in Kandla Export: orders not specifically enumerated under Order Forty Three are not appealable.
scenes.shown: The Supreme Court affirmed this view in Kandla Export: orders not specifically enumerated under Order XLIII are not appealable.

scenes.dialogue: Order Forty Three provides no appeal against converting a summary suit into a regular suit. So both appeals were dismissed as not maintainable.
scenes.shown: Order XLIII provides no appeal against converting a summary suit into a regular suit. So both appeals were dismissed as not maintainable.
